defect: parse_block_expression and parse_closure_expression skip working_set.exit_scope() whenever a block/closure lacks a closing '}' (is_closed == false) to preserve local variables for incomplete-input completion, while parse_paren_expr speculatively calls parse_full_cell_path on bare-word interpolations like `(do {0})-str` and truncates parse_errors on ParseError::Unclosed without restoring working_set.delta.scope. Subsequent command definitions in the same REPL entry then land inside the leaked inner scope instead of the top-level scope merged into EngineState.
trigger: Defining a command whose body contains a bare-word interpolation starting with a parenthesized block/closure expression, such as `def cmd [] { (do {0})-str }; cmd`, then invoking `cmd` in a subsequent REPL entry.
match_rule: Identify that skipping working_set.exit_scope() when is_closed is false in parse_block_expression/parse_closure_expression leaks scopes across parse_paren_expr's speculative parse_full_cell_path fallback, because parse_paren_expr truncates parse_errors on Unclosed without unwinding working_set.delta.scope.
near_misses: Complaining generally about incomplete-input completion keeping scopes open or parse_paren_expr error truncation without linking the un-exited scope from parse_block_expression/parse_closure_expression to parse_paren_expr's speculative fallback.
why_findable: 5b0800a14 guards working_set.exit_scope() behind `if is_closed` in parse_block_expression, parse_match_block_expression, and parse_closure_expression, while parse_paren_expr in the same file speculatively calls parse_full_cell_path and recovers from ParseError::Unclosed by only calling working_set.parse_errors.truncate(starting_error_count).
notes: Fix commit 34d3301a (after parser file split f70ed723) captures starting_scope_count before parse_full_cell_path in parse_paren_expr and exits leaked scopes on malformed_subexpr fallback.

defect: LanguageServer::new_engine_state hardcodes `$env.PWD` to the relative path "." instead of std::env::current_dir(), replacing the absolute path previously set at each call site. EngineState::cwd validates PWD with AbsolutePathBuf::try_from and rejects relative paths with "$env.PWD is not an absolute path", causing false diagnostics when the LSP parses scripts using parse-time path commands such as `const toolkit_dir = path self .`.
trigger: Opening a Nushell script containing `const toolkit_dir = path self .` (or another parse-time command calling EngineState::cwd) in nu-lsp.
match_rule: Identify that LanguageServer::new_engine_state sets PWD to relative "." instead of an absolute directory path, causing EngineState::cwd to fail AbsolutePathBuf validation during LSP parsing/diagnostics.
near_misses: Commenting only on Value::test_string usage or missing workspace folder handling without identifying that relative "." violates EngineState::cwd's absolute-path invariant.
why_findable: The diff replaces `std::env::current_dir()` with `Value::test_string(".")` in new_engine_state, while EngineState::cwd in crates/nu-protocol/src/engine/engine_state.rs:956 explicitly fails with "$env.PWD is not an absolute path" for any non-absolute PWD.
notes: Fix commit 0b71eb20 restores `std::env::current_dir()` in new_engine_state and adds diagnostics fixture pwd.nu.

defect: ExpandedTable::build_list sets clip_columns: false for top-level lists and maybe_expand_table routes overflowing tables (total_width > term_width) to NuTable::draw(term_width), where DimensionCtrl::change -> width_ctrl_truncate applies plain-text Width::wrap / Width::truncate to every undersized column. Because expanded list cells can contain pre-rendered nested box-drawing tables from expand_entry_with_header, wrapping or truncating those cells as flat strings slices through their box borders and corrupts nested table layout.
trigger: Running `table --expand` (e.g. `plugin list`) on a table containing nested subtables when total width exceeds terminal width under wrapping or truncating trim strategy.
match_rule: Identify that routing unclipped ExpandedTable output through NuTable::draw / DimensionCtrl::change applies plain-text wrapping or truncation directly to cells containing pre-rendered nested tables, breaking their box borders instead of re-rendering/constraining the inner table.
near_misses: Flagging general column width calculation, header_on_separator, or scalar text wrapping without identifying that pre-rendered nested table strings are being wrapped/truncated as plain text.
why_findable: The diff switches top-level build_list to clip_columns: false and routes overflowing tables in maybe_expand_table to NuTable::draw, which invokes width_ctrl_truncate uniformly on all cell strings in table.rs even though expand_list populates cells with already-rendered multi-line nested tables.
notes: Fix commit 164c9f2e tracks nested_cells in NuTable so width_ctrl_truncate skips raw text wrapping on them and instead re-renders inner tables to the fitted column width.

defect: UMkdir::run invokes uu_mkdir::mkdir with `recursive: IS_RECURSIVE` (true), which succeeds with Ok(()) when a target directory already exists, yet the verbose Ok branch unconditionally records `"created" => Value::bool(true, call.head)` without checking whether the directory already existed before the call.
trigger: Running `mkdir -v existing_dir` on a directory that already exists.
match_rule: Identify that UMkdir::run calls mkdir with recursive: true (which returns Ok(()) for existing directories) and unconditionally sets `created: true` in the verbose output record instead of checking prior existence.
near_misses: Complaining about TOCTOU races or whether mkdir should return an error on existing directories rather than reporting `created: false`.
why_findable: In the same function in umkdir.rs, config sets `recursive: IS_RECURSIVE` (const true at line 9), and the `else if is_verbose` arm hardcodes `"created" => Value::bool(true, call.head)` for every Ok(()) result.
notes: Local control (single function + file-local const IS_RECURSIVE). Fix commit b6e6562a checks `let already_existed = dir.exists()` before calling mkdir.

defect: create_pool caches and reuses a single Arc<rayon::ThreadPool> per num_threads for all top-level par-each invocations (only bypassing the cache when rayon::current_thread_index().is_some()), while stream_parallel_values spawns the producer onto that pool via pool.spawn(...) feeding a bounded mpsc::sync_channel(64). When two streaming par-each stages with the same thread count are chained in a pipeline (both created on the main evaluator thread), they share the same pool; once the upstream channel fills, upstream workers block on tx.send while the downstream consumer cannot be scheduled on the saturated pool, deadlocking.
trigger: Chaining two streaming par-each stages with the same `--threads` count over more than STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE (64) values, e.g. `0..99 | par-each --threads 1 {|it| $it } | par-each --threads 1 {|it| $it }`.
match_rule: Identify that chained top-level streaming par-each stages with the same thread count reuse the same cached pool from THREAD_POOLS (since create_pool only bypasses the cache for nested Rayon worker calls), causing pool starvation / deadlock on the bounded sync_channel when stream_parallel_values spawns both stages onto that shared pool.
near_misses: Flagging only nested par-each calls or Rayon's global pool (which c1675b75 already avoided) without identifying chained sibling pipeline stages reusing the same cached pool.
why_findable: c1675b75 switches stream_parallel_values from rayon::spawn to pool.spawn on the cached pool returned by create_pool, which only checks rayon::current_thread_index().is_some() and hands out identical Arc<ThreadPool> handles to concurrently streaming top-level pipeline stages.
notes: Fix commit 54c09e9a only reuses cached pools when Arc::strong_count(pool) == 1 (idle) and keeps the pool Arc alive inside the spawned producer until completion.

defect: find_reference_in_file pushes `working_set.get_variable(*vid).declaration_span` directly into the reference spans used by LSP rename. Because nu-parser stores the full flag token including its leading `--` in `declaration_span` for named flag parameters (e.g. `--foo: int`), replacing that span with the bare new variable name strips the leading `--` and turns the flag into a positional parameter.
trigger: Running LSP rename on a custom command's named flag parameter (e.g. renaming `$param` / `--param` in `export def foooo [--param: int] { $param }`).
match_rule: Identify that pushing Variable.declaration_span directly into rename reference ranges includes the leading `--` prefix of flag parameter declarations, so LSP rename overwrites `--flag` with the bare new name and corrupts the command signature.
near_misses: Flagging missing variable references in `use` commands, module rename limitations, or `$` prefix handling on variable usages without identifying leading `--` on flag parameter declaration_span.
why_findable: workspace.rs pushes `working_set.get_variable(*vid).declaration_span` verbatim as a rename edit range, while nu-parser's parse_full_signature records flag variable declaration_span starting at `--`.
notes: Fix commit 84c720da counts leading `b'-'` bytes in decl_span and advances the edit start past them.

defect: EvalContext::collect_reg calls `check_exit_status_future(data.exit)?` before draining `data.body.into_value(span)` when experimental `pipefail` is enabled. Because check_exit_status_future waits for the external child process to exit while data.body holds the unread stdout pipe, any external command writing more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) blocks on stdout write and deadlocks forever.
trigger: With `--experimental-options=[pipefail]`, assigning the output of an external command that writes >64 KiB to stdout to a variable, e.g. `let x = cat a_large_file.txt`.
match_rule: Identify that calling check_exit_status_future(data.exit) before draining data.body (into_value) in EvalContext::collect_reg deadlocks when an external command's stdout fills the OS pipe buffer and blocks waiting for the reader before exiting.
near_misses: Complaining generally about pipefail error ordering or dropping exit status without identifying the pipe-buffer deadlock from waiting for child exit before draining stdout.
why_findable: 1025ddb3 inserts `check_exit_status_future(data.exit)?` directly before `data.body.into_value(span)` in collect_reg, whereas check_exit_status_future in nu-protocol::process waits on process termination and sibling drain sites in eval_ir.rs (line 1597-1601) drain data.body before waiting on data.exit.
notes: Fix commit e705408c evaluates `let result = body.into_value(span);` before calling `check_exit_status_future(data.exit)?`.

defect: The CompareTypes refactor replaces PipelineData::is_subtype_of (which delegated PipelineData::Value directly to Value::is_subtype_of) with `self.get_type().is_assignable_to(dst)` and `self.get_type().compare_types(other)`. Calling `get_type()` on a concrete `PipelineData::Value` widens heterogeneous values (e.g., a list of records with mixed columns such as `[{a: 1, b: 2}, {a: 1}]` becoming `Type::List(Type::OneOf(...))`) instead of using `Value`'s more accurate structural `CompareTypes` implementation, causing valid runtime `PipelineData::Value` inputs to fail runtime type checks.
trigger: Passing a concrete runtime `PipelineData::Value` whose widened `get_type()` is less precise than `Value::is_assignable_to` (for example, a heterogeneous list of records like `[{a: 1, b: 2}, {a: 1}]` checked against `table<a: int>` or `table`) through a runtime `PipelineData::is_assignable_to` / `compare_types` check.
match_rule: Identify that `CompareTypes<Type> for PipelineData` (`compare_types` and `is_assignable_to`) dropped direct delegation of `PipelineData::Value(val, _)` to `Value`'s `CompareTypes` methods by routing everything through `self.get_type()`, regressing runtime type checks on concrete values.
near_misses: Flagging only ListStream or ByteStream type handling without identifying the dropped `PipelineData::Value` delegation to `Value::is_assignable_to` / `Value::compare_types`.
why_findable: The diff deletes `PipelineData::is_subtype_of`'s `(PipelineData::Value(val, ..), ty) => val.is_subtype_of(ty)` arm in favor of `self.get_type().is_assignable_to(dst)`, while `crates/nu-protocol/src/value/mod.rs` in the same diff defines `impl CompareTypes<Type> for Value` specifically to perform more accurate structural value-level type checking than `Value::get_type()`.
notes: Fix commit 69e3a661 delegates PipelineData::Value to value.compare_types/is_assignable_to and delegates non-Record list elements in Table<->List comparisons to Type::Record(table_cols). | no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: Signature::get_output_type infers a command's parse-time output type by filtering input_output_types with `input.is_assignable_to(in_ty)` and unioning all matching outputs. Because Type::is_assignable_to in ty.rs treats every Type::Custom(_) as assignable to Type::List(_), Type::Table(_), and Type::Record(_) (so cell-path commands like `get` type-check), piping a custom value such as `semver` into a command with structured pairs like `into string` matches only `(list, list)`, `(table, table)`, `(record, record)` and infers `oneof<list<string>, table, record>` instead of `string`, breaking typed assignments and calls.
trigger: Evaluating `let s = "1.0.0" | into semver | into string` or passing `("1.0.0" | into semver | into string)` to a command expecting `string` such as `path join`.
match_rule: Identify that Signature::get_output_type unions every input_output_types pair where input.is_assignable_to(in_ty), interacting with Type::Custom(_)'s wildcard assignability to List/Table/Record in ty.rs so commands like `into string` infer `oneof<list<string>, table, record>` for custom values like `semver` instead of `string`.
near_misses: Complaining generally about Type::OneOf widening or missing input_output_types entries on unrelated commands without connecting Signature::get_output_type to Type::Custom's structured-type assignability in ty.rs.
why_findable: b62861dd adds Signature::get_output_type using `input.is_assignable_to(in_ty)` while crates/nu-protocol/src/ty.rs:348 explicitly defines `(Type::List(_) | Type::Table(_) | Type::Record(_), Type::Custom(_)) => true`, and crates/nu-command/src/conversions/into/string.rs declares list/table/record pairs without custom pairs.
notes: Fix commit f7e1850a adds semver/semver-range -> string pairs to IntoString and skips custom-to-structured fallback pairs in Signature::get_output_type when a real lattice match exists.

defect: The idx runtime serializes and deserializes `item.is_deleted()` tombstones in snapshot export/import, yet idx_status_from_picker reports raw `picker.get_files().len()` / `picker.get_dirs().len()` and stream_dirs / stream_files iterate `picker.get_dirs()` / `picker.get_files()` without filtering `!item.is_deleted()`. Deleted files and directories therefore remain visible in `idx status`, `idx files`, `idx dirs`, and exported snapshots.
trigger: Deleting a file or directory from a watched `idx` index and running `idx status`, `idx files`, `idx dirs`, or `idx export`.
match_rule: Identify that idx_status_from_picker, stream_dirs, stream_files (and/or snapshot export/import) read picker.get_files()/get_dirs() without filtering out tombstoned entries where `item.is_deleted()` is true, despite state.rs already tracking `is_deleted` in its snapshot code.
near_misses: Flagging lock contention, arena_bytes accounting, or watcher startup timeouts without identifying missing `!item.is_deleted()` filtering on tombstoned entries.
why_findable: In the same file crates/nu-command/src/filesystem/idx/state.rs introduced by 6983c918, snapshot export explicitly calls `item.is_deleted()` (line 754) and stores `is_deleted` in SQLite (line 804), while sibling query functions idx_status_from_picker, stream_dirs, and stream_files count and emit every element of get_files()/get_dirs() unfiltered.
notes: Fix commit 0385840f uses picker.live_file_count() and filters `!item.is_deleted()` across status, stream_dirs, stream_files, export, and import.

defect: CommandWideCompletion::fetch evaluates custom `@complete` command blocks with `nu_engine::eval_block::<WithoutDebug>` instead of `nu_engine::eval_block_with_early_return::<WithoutDebug>`. Because eval_block surfaces explicit `return <expr>` statements as `Err(ShellError::Return { .. })`, any command-wide completer using `return` fails evaluation and silently yields no completions.
trigger: Defining a `@complete` command-wide completer that uses an explicit `return` statement, e.g. `def "nu-complete foo" [spans: list] { return ($spans ++ [some more]) }`, and completing `foo bar baz`.
match_rule: Identify that CommandWideCompletion::fetch calls nu_engine::eval_block instead of nu_engine::eval_block_with_early_return, causing explicit `return` statements inside `@complete` completers to fail with ShellError::Return and drop completion suggestions.
near_misses: Flagging stack capture setup, span offsets, or external completers without identifying eval_block vs eval_block_with_early_return for explicit `return`.
why_findable: CommandWideCompletion::fetch calls `nu_engine::eval_block` directly on a custom command's block (line 274), whereas crates/nu-engine/src/eval.rs defines `eval_block_with_early_return` specifically to catch `ShellError::Return` for custom command invocations (and sibling `CustomCompletion` calls `eval_call`, which handles early return).
notes: Fix commit 940a4ec4 changes eval_block to eval_block_with_early_return in CommandWideCompletion::fetch.

defect: Non-blocking completions move all Tab completion execution onto a background CompletionWorker thread using `isolated_stack(..., background: true)` which sets `stack.suppress_stdin()`. Interactive completers that need the TTY—such as `input list` (which checks `require_stdin` and declines when stdin is suppressed) or external pickers like `fzf`—either fail and fall back to file completion or race reedline for `/dev/tty` and leave the REPL hung.
trigger: Pressing Tab when `$env.config.completions.external.completer` or a custom `@complete` / `@comp` closure invokes `input list` or `^fzf`.
match_rule: Identify that running user/external completion closures on the background completion worker with `stack.suppress_stdin()` breaks interactive TTY pickers (`input list`, `fzf`) because stdin is suppressed / detached from the foreground REPL terminal.
near_misses: Flagging only cache staleness or repaint timing without identifying background-thread execution + `suppress_stdin` breaking interactive completers like `input list` / `fzf`.
why_findable: 1ba3edbaa routes every completion query unconditionally through the background worker with `stack.suppress_stdin()`, while crates/nu-command/src/platform/input/list.rs requires live stdin/TTY and external commands like `fzf` spawned with piped stdin skip `setsid` and race reedline on `/dev/tty`.
notes: Fix commit 1e6f2d2b runs user/external completers synchronously on the REPL thread with terminal raw-mode restoration while keeping file/command completions non-blocking.

defect: In the experimental dc-glob branch of `glob_from`, the literal-path fast path checks `if pattern_path.exists() && !pattern_path.is_dir()`, passing plain existing directory paths to `nu_glob::dc_glob::glob_from_interruptible`. Because dc-glob's traversal calls `read_dir` on the pattern directory and iterates its children instead of emitting the directory itself, commands like `rm -r subdir` and `cp -r subdir dest` receive empty or wrong matches and fail to remove/copy literal directories.
trigger: With `--experimental-options=[dc-glob]`, running `rm -r subdir` or `cp -r subdir dest` on an existing literal directory path without glob metacharacters.
match_rule: Identify that guarding the dc-glob literal-path fast path in `glob_from` with `!pattern_path.is_dir()` sends existing literal directories into dc-glob's traversal, which enumerates directory contents via `read_dir` instead of yielding the directory itself (breaking `rm -r` / `cp -r`).
near_misses: Flagging only symlink handling or glob metacharacter parsing without identifying that `!pattern_path.is_dir()` breaks literal existing directory paths under dc-glob.
why_findable: 5efa5459 adds `if pattern_path.exists() && !pattern_path.is_dir()` in crates/nu-engine/src/glob_from.rs while its dc-glob traversal engine in crates/nu-glob/src/dc_glob/ calls read_dir on the resolved directory rather than emitting the start directory for a literal pattern.
notes: Fix commit 7a466792 removes `&& !pattern_path.is_dir()` so any existing literal path is returned directly.

defect: compile_binary_op sets `lhs_reg = out_reg` and forwards `in_reg` directly as `rhs_in_reg` to `compile_expression` whenever `rhs.has_in_variable(working_set)` is true. When the caller reuses the same register for input and output (`in_reg == Some(out_reg)`, so `in_reg == lhs_reg`), compiling an RHS that collects `$in` (e.g. `not $in` or `[$in]`) emits a `Drop` instruction on `rhs_in_reg`, freeing the still-live `lhs_reg` and triggering a `register_uninitialized` compile error on the subsequent BinaryOp.
trigger: Compiling a binary operation where input and output registers alias and the RHS collects `$in`, such as `[1 2] | where true and not $in`.
match_rule: Identify that compile_binary_op forwards `in_reg` directly to RHS compilation without cloning when `in_reg == Some(lhs_reg)` (since `lhs_reg = out_reg`), allowing RHS `drop_input` paths in compile_expression to drop the live LHS register and cause `register_uninitialized`.
near_misses: Flagging general `$in` vs `$it` semantics in `where` or short-circuit branch labels without identifying the register aliasing (`in_reg == lhs_reg == out_reg`) where RHS drops the live LHS register.
why_findable: f7b85d03 adds `in_reg` to `compile_binary_op` and passes it uncloned to both LHS and RHS while `lhs_reg = out_reg`, and sibling callers in crates/nu-engine/src/compile/expression.rs pass `in_reg == Some(out_reg)` while `compile_expression` emits `Drop` on its `in_reg`.
notes: Fix commit 8b995956 clones `in_reg` via `builder.clone_reg` when `in_reg == Some(lhs_reg)` in both the short-circuit (`and`/`or`) and general binary-op branches.

defect: parse_unit_value checks `bytes[0] == b'.'` without verifying `bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()`, so non-numeric bare words starting with a dot and ending in a unit suffix (such as `.foons` inside `[.foons]`) bypass the early return, match the `ns` unit suffix, and fail to parse as a number instead of being treated as a string.
trigger: Parsing a bare word starting with `.` and ending with a duration/filesize unit suffix, such as `[.foons]`.
match_rule: Identify that `bytes[0] == b'.'` in parse_unit_value lacks `&& bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()`, causing dot-prefixed bare words ending in a unit suffix like `.foons` to enter unit parsing and error.
near_misses: Complaining about negative numbers or UTF-8 slicing without identifying the missing `bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()` guard on `bytes[0] == b'.'`.
why_findable: Right on the next line of the same condition, `b'-'` checks `bytes[0] == b'-' && bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()`, whereas the newly added `bytes[0] == b'.'` omits `bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()`.
notes: Local control (single condition in parse_unit_value). Fix commit e70202b0 adds `&& bytes[1].is_ascii_digit()`.

defect: parse_range computes `paren_depth` via unchecked usize subtraction `before.chars().filter(|&c| c == '(').count() - before.chars().filter(|&c| c == ')').count()`, which panics with arithmetic underflow whenever an unmatched `)` precedes `..`.
trigger: Parsing an input containing an unmatched closing parenthesis before `..`, e.g. `)0..1` or `1)..2`.
match_rule: Identify that subtracting `')'` count from `'('` count with unchecked `-` on `usize` in parse_range underflows and panics when there are more `)` than `(` before `..`.
near_misses: Complaining about nested quotes or bracket depth rather than the unchecked usize subtraction underflow on unmatched `)`.
why_findable: Directly visible in the single 2-line subtraction expression introduced in parse_range.
notes: Local control (single expression in parse_range). Fix commit 13067f13 uses `.checked_sub(...)`.

defect: stream_parallel_values spawns the streaming par-each producer onto Rayon's global thread pool via `rayon::spawn(...)` with a bounded `mpsc::sync_channel(64)` while ParEach::run also executes default-thread (`--threads` omitted) work on Rayon's global pool. When an upstream command that also uses Rayon's global pool (such as `ls` with `par_bridge()` or experimental `dc-glob`) feeds `par-each`, pool workers block on channel sends/receives while waiting for free workers in the same global pool, causing a deadlock.
trigger: Piping a Rayon-backed streaming command into streaming `par-each`, e.g. `ls | wrap name | par-each {}` or `glob '*' | wrap name | par-each {}`.
match_rule: Identify that stream_parallel_values spawns its producer on Rayon's shared global pool (`rayon::spawn`) with a bounded sync_channel, deadlocking when an upstream producer (`ls`, `dc-glob`) or nested `par-each` also schedules work on Rayon's global pool.
near_misses: Flagging only `--keep-order` or signal checking without identifying Rayon global thread-pool starvation / deadlock between `stream_parallel_values` (`rayon::spawn`) and upstream Rayon-backed streams.
why_findable: 8a5a9ae1 introduces bounded-channel streaming via `rayon::spawn` in par_each.rs, while sibling command `ls` (crates/nu-command/src/filesystem/ls.rs) already streams via Rayon's global pool (`par_bridge`), causing shared-pool deadlock.
notes: Fix commit c1675b75 gives par-each dedicated thread pools (never using Rayon's global pool) and switches `rayon::spawn` to `pool.spawn`.

defect: DotNuCompletion::fetch builds completion descriptions for already-loaded modules by joining raw comment spans (`working_set.get_span_contents(*sp)`) directly with `"\n"`, leaving raw `#` comment prefixes, leading indentation, and extra documentation paragraphs verbatim instead of formatting them via `working_set.build_desc(spans).0` as `help modules` does.
trigger: Tab-completing a loaded module with `#` doc comments (e.g. `use c<tab>` for stdlib `clip` or a custom module with `# comment`).
match_rule: Identify that DotNuCompletion::fetch concatenates raw comment span bytes via working_set.get_span_contents instead of formatting module comments with working_set.build_desc, exposing raw `#` markers and indentation in completion descriptions.
near_misses: Flagging only unimported/inline modules (which the commit already notes in a TODO) without identifying raw `#` comment span joining vs working_set.build_desc.
why_findable: 644da8b1 calls `working_set.get_module_comments(*module_id)` and manually joins raw span bytes, while `StateWorkingSet::build_desc` in crates/nu-protocol/src/engine/state_working_set.rs (and callers in `help modules`) is the standard helper that strips `#` prefixes and separates description from extra description.
notes: Fix commit 75cccd39 replaces manual span joining with `working_set.build_desc(spans).0` and updates module_name_completions / exportable_completions tests.

defect: LanguageServer::find_location_by_span moved `if !path.is_file() { return None; }` to AFTER `let target_uri = path_to_uri(path);`. Because `path_to_uri` in crates/nu-lsp/src/lib.rs calls `Url::from_file_path(path).expect(...)` which panics on any relative path, and standard-library virtual files (e.g. `std/assert`) are cached in working_set.files() with relative names, invoking go-to-definition on a stdlib symbol panics the LSP server.
trigger: Running LSP goto-definition on a symbol imported from the standard library, e.g. `use std/assert` and jumping to `assert`.
match_rule: Identify that moving the `path.is_file()` guard after `path_to_uri(path)` in goto.rs causes `path_to_uri` (in nu-lsp/src/lib.rs) to panic on relative virtual file paths such as cached `nu-std` files.
near_misses: Flagging missing vendor std-lib resolution or unsaved buffer lookup without identifying that `path_to_uri` panics on relative paths when called before filtering non-absolute/virtual paths.
why_findable: e1ce67e3c removes `if !path.is_file() { return None; }` from right above `path_to_uri(path)` in goto.rs, while `path_to_uri` in crates/nu-lsp/src/lib.rs unwraps `Url::from_file_path` (which returns `Err` for relative paths like stdlib virtual files).
notes: Fix commit d1a82495 checks `if path.is_relative()` before calling `path_to_uri(path)` and adds test `goto_definition_on_stdlib_should_not_panic`.

defect: find_header_positions records UTF-8 byte offsets of column starts in the header line via `char_indices()`, and split_line_by_positions directly slices each data line with `&line[start..actual_end]`. Because byte offsets that fall on character boundaries in the header line can land in the middle of a multibyte UTF-8 character on a data line, `detect columns` panics with a byte-index-not-char-boundary error on Unicode inputs.
trigger: Piping text with ASCII headers and multibyte Unicode characters in data rows (so a header column byte offset falls inside a multibyte character) into `detect columns`.
match_rule: Identify that split_line_by_positions slices data lines (`&line[start..actual_end]`) using byte offsets computed by find_header_positions from the header line without checking `is_char_boundary`, panicking on multibyte UTF-8 data.
near_misses: Flagging only display width vs byte length misalignment without identifying the UTF-8 char-boundary slicing panic in `&line[start..actual_end]`.
why_findable: e8456592 introduces both find_header_positions (emitting byte indices from header_line.char_indices()) and split_line_by_positions (directly indexing `&line[start..actual_end]` on different data rows with the mistaken comment that header char boundaries are safe for data lines).
notes: Fix commit f036bdf6 adjusts slice indices to valid UTF-8 char boundaries before slicing.

defect: nu_utils::quoting::as_raw_string picks `hash_count` by checking only `!s.contains(&format!("'", "#".repeat(hash_count)))`, without checking whether `s` begins with `#` (`!s.starts_with(&hashes)`). When a string starts with `#` (e.g. a TOML/script comment `# example.toml`), as_raw_string emits `r#'# example.toml'#`, which nu-parser's raw-string lexer parses as immediately closed after the opening quote (`r#'#`) followed by invalid trailing tokens.
trigger: Serializing a string starting with `#` via `to nuon --raw-strings` (e.g. `"# example.toml\nname = \"my-app\"" | to nuon --raw-strings`) and parsing it back.
match_rule: Identify that as_raw_string only checks `!s.contains(&closing)` (`'#...#`) and omits checking whether `s` starts with `#` (e.g. `!s.starts_with(&hashes)`), producing `r#'#...'#` which Nushell's raw-string lexer rejects or terminates early.
near_misses: Flagging trailing quotes, control characters, or empty strings without identifying strings starting with `#` colliding with the `r#'` delimiter.
why_findable: 99c5c5f9 adds as_raw_string in crates/nu-utils/src/quoting.rs checking only `!s.contains(&closing)`, while Nushell's raw-string lexer in crates/nu-parser/src/lex.rs treats `'<N hashes>` immediately after the opening `'` as the closing delimiter when content starts with `#`.
notes: Fix commit 124d39ef adds `!s.starts_with(&hashes)` to the loop condition in as_raw_string.

defect: IdxImport::run enabled filesystem watching by default (`watch = !no_watch`) and passed `watch` into `restore_snapshot`, which starts a live watched FFF FilePicker while still storing `snapshot_files: Some(...)` and `snapshot_dirs: Some(...)` in IdxRuntime. Because `stream_files`, `stream_dirs`, `stream_find`, and `current_status` prefer restored snapshot rows whenever present whereas `stream_grep` (`idx search`) queries the live `shared_picker`, watched imports enter a split-brain state where newly created files appear in `idx search` but never appear in `idx files`, `idx dirs`, `idx find`, or `idx status`.
trigger: Running `idx import <snapshot>` (with default watch enabled), creating a new file in the indexed directory, and querying `idx files` / `idx dirs` / `idx find` / `idx status` vs `idx search`.
match_rule: Identify that enabling watching on `idx import` while `restore_snapshot` still populates `snapshot_files`/`snapshot_dirs` causes `stream_files`/`stream_dirs`/`stream_find`/`current_status` to keep serving stale snapshot rows while `stream_grep` reads the live watched picker.
near_misses: Flagging only `idx import --no-watch` or SQLite schema mismatches without identifying the split-brain between snapshot-backed read paths and the live watched picker.
why_findable: c19a069d2 enables `watch` in IdxImport::run -> restore_snapshot without clearing snapshot mode, while sibling functions `stream_files`, `stream_dirs`, `stream_find`, and `current_status` in the same file state.rs branch on `snapshot_files.is_some()` instead of reading `shared_picker`.
notes: Fix commit edb7010c routes watched `idx import` through the live initialization path and reserves snapshot rows for `--no-watch`.

defect: In crates/nuon/src/to.rs, the `Value::Closure` branch under `serialize_types` (`to nuon --serialize`) returns raw unquoted closure source text (`contents_string.to_string()`) instead of quoting and escaping it with `escape_quote_string(...)` like sibling string/serialized branches. As a result, `to nuon --serialize` emits raw `{|| ...}` syntax that is invalid NUON and fails when parsed back by `from nuon`.
trigger: Running `{|x| $x + 1} | to nuon --serialize | from nuon`.
match_rule: Identify that `value_to_string` in nuon/src/to.rs returns unquoted closure text for `Value::Closure` when `serialize_types` is true instead of calling `escape_quote_string`, producing invalid NUON that `from nuon` cannot deserialize.
near_misses: Flagging closure error messages without `--serialize` or `to json`/`to toml` serialization without identifying the missing quoting/escaping in nuon's `value_to_string`.
why_findable: dad956b2 adds the `serialize_types` branch for `Value::Closure` returning raw `contents_string.to_string()` directly inside `nuon/src/to.rs`, where sibling branches (`Value::String`, etc.) use `escape_quote_string` so `crates/nuon/src/from.rs` can parse the result as a NUON string.
notes: Fix commit 7a6cfa24 wraps the serialized closure string in `escape_quote_string(...)`.

defect: CHAR_MAP in crates/nu-command/src/strings/char_.rs inserts `"lsep" => LINE_SEPARATOR_CHAR.to_string()` at line 70, but leaves the old duplicate entry `"lsep" => '\n'.to_string()` two lines below at line 72, overwriting the platform-agnostic separator with `'\n'` on Windows.
trigger: Evaluating `char lsep` on Windows (where `LINE_SEPARATOR_CHAR` is `"\r\n"`).
match_rule: Identify that CHAR_MAP defines duplicate key `"lsep"`, so the second entry `"lsep" => '\n'.to_string()` overwrites `"lsep" => LINE_SEPARATOR_CHAR.to_string()`.
near_misses: Flagging `char eol` or `char line_sep` rather than the duplicate `"lsep"` entry.
why_findable: Both `"lsep"` entries appear within 3 lines of each other in the same IndexMap literal.
notes: Local control (single map literal). Fix commit bfe398ca deletes the duplicate `"lsep" => '\n'.to_string()` line.

defect: rm() was changed to capture the first `Err(err)` from the deletion iterator into `cmd_result` and return it, without checking `force && matches!(err, ShellError::Io(IoError { kind: NotFound, .. }))`. Even though `--force` (`-f`) is documented and handled earlier in `rm()` to suppress missing-file errors, `rm -f` now fails when a target disappears or is not found during removal.
trigger: Running `rm -f` on targets where one disappears or is not found during removal (e.g. removing a directory and its symlink in one `rm -f` call).
match_rule: Identify that capturing iterator errors into `cmd_result` in `rm()` ignores the `--force` flag for `ErrorKind::NotFound`, causing `rm -f` to return an error instead of suppressing not-found errors.
near_misses: Flagging error reporting order for multiple errors or permission errors without identifying `force` + `NotFound` suppression.
why_findable: Inside the same `fn rm` function, `force` is read at line 114 and used to suppress `ErrorKind::NotFound` at line 302, while the newly added `cmd_result = Err(err)` at line 468 ignores `force`.
notes: Local control (within `fn rm`). Fix commit 3abe3887 guards `cmd_result = Err(err)` with `if !(force && matches!(err, ShellError::Io(IoError { kind: Std(NotFound), .. })))`.

defect: External::run hoisted `let paths = nu_engine::env::path_str(engine_state, stack, call.head)?;` above the Windows CMD-builtin and absolute-path checks. Because `nu_engine::env::path_str` in crates/nu-engine/src/env.rs returns `Err(ShellError::EnvVarNotFoundAtRuntime)` whenever `$env.PATH` is unset, running a Windows CMD builtin or an explicit/absolute external executable after `hide-env PATH` fails immediately with a PATH-not-found error.
trigger: Running `hide-env PATH` and then invoking an external command by absolute path (or a Windows CMD builtin).
match_rule: Identify that hoisting `nu_engine::env::path_str(...)?` before the Windows CMD builtin and path-resolution branches causes External::run to fail with EnvVarNotFoundAtRuntime whenever `$env.PATH` is unset, breaking absolute-path commands and CMD builtins.
near_misses: Flagging only performance of calling `which` twice on Windows without identifying that `?` on `path_str` aborts execution when `$env.PATH` is missing.
why_findable: 237a6856 moves `path_str(...)?` from the `else` branch (line 136) to unconditional line 81 before the `if cfg!(windows)` / builtin / explicit-path branches, while `nu_engine::env::path_str` in crates/nu-engine/src/env.rs returns `Err` when `PATH` is absent.
notes: Fix commit 038f8f85 changes `?` to `.unwrap_or_default()`.

defect: parse_row_condition added `working_set.enter_scope()` at entry and `working_set.exit_scope()` at the bottom, but left three early `return` paths in the middle (`Expr::FullCellPath`, `Expr::Var`, and type-mismatch garbage return) without calling `working_set.exit_scope()`. Whenever `where $cond` uses a stored closure variable or triggers a type error, a parser scope leaks and breaks subsequent declarations/exports.
trigger: Using a stored closure variable in `where` inside a module or block, e.g. `let cond = {|x| $x > 1}; [1 2] | where $cond`, followed by another `export def`.
match_rule: Identify that the three early `return` branches in `parse_row_condition` (FullCellPath, Var, and type-mismatch error) skip `working_set.exit_scope()`, leaking the scope opened at the start of `parse_row_condition`.
near_misses: Complaining generally about `$it` variable shadowing without identifying the missing `working_set.exit_scope()` on the early returns in `parse_row_condition`.
why_findable: The 15-line intro commit adds `enter_scope()` at line 4007 and `exit_scope()` at line 4061 of the same function while three `return` statements sit between lines 4035 and 4055.
notes: Local control (single function `parse_row_condition`). Fix commit 679b2e2a adds `working_set.exit_scope()` before all three early returns.

defect: 7b6e1afe changed dc-glob's compiler/matcher so bare `**` yields the start directory itself (matching the empty relative path). However, `ls_for_one_pattern` in crates/nu-command/src/filesystem/ls.rs strips `prefix` from each matched path and joins `new_prefix.join(remainder)`, producing an empty string `""` instead of `"."` for the start directory entry when running `ls **` under dc-glob.
trigger: Running `ls **` with `--experimental-options=[dc-glob]`.
match_rule: Identify that making dc-glob emit the start directory itself for bare `**` causes `ls_for_one_pattern` in ls.rs to strip the prefix down to an empty relative path `""` instead of `"."` (and/or mis-handle bare `**` directory emission in `ls`).
near_misses: Flagging symlink cycles or permission errors in dc-glob without connecting bare `**` emitting the start directory to `ls_for_one_pattern` producing an empty path.
why_findable: 7b6e1afe explicitly changes dc-glob so bare `**` emits the start directory (empty relative path), while crates/nu-command/src/filesystem/ls.rs:542 unconditionally computes `new_prefix.join(remainder).to_string_lossy()` without mapping an empty joined path to `"."`.
notes: Fix commit 58a64734 maps an empty joined path in ls.rs to `"."` and fixes bare `**` compilation/tests.

defect: Where::signature changed the `condition` parameter shape from `SyntaxShape::RowCondition` to `SyntaxShape::OneOf(vec![SyntaxShape::RowCondition, SyntaxShape::Closure(Some(vec![SyntaxShape::Any]))])`. Because `nu-parser`'s `parse_multispan_value` / `SyntaxShape::OneOf` tries `RowCondition` first (which consumes all remaining tokens into a multi-span expression) and on parse error retries `Closure` on the same tokens, invalid arguments to `where` produce multiple AST expressions with overlapping spans, causing `nu-highlight` to duplicate text.
trigger: Syntax-highlighting a `where` command with invalid arguments, e.g. `"where a b" | nu-highlight`.
match_rule: Identify that wrapping `SyntaxShape::RowCondition` together with `SyntaxShape::Closure` inside `SyntaxShape::OneOf` in `Where::signature` interacts badly with `nu-parser`'s multi-span `OneOf` parsing (since `RowCondition` already consumes all spans and accepts closures), creating overlapping AST spans that duplicate highlighted text.
near_misses: Flagging runtime `where` evaluation or `$it` scoping without identifying the `SyntaxShape::OneOf([RowCondition, Closure])` interaction with multi-span parsing/highlighting.
why_findable: e0eb29f1 both adds `Expr::Var` / `Expr::FullCellPath` closure support directly inside `parse_row_condition` AND wraps `RowCondition` in `SyntaxShape::OneOf([RowCondition, Closure])` in `where_.rs`, while `crates/nu-parser/src/parser.rs` parses `OneOf` by retrying alternatives over spans already consumed by `RowCondition`.
notes: Fix commit 51265b26 reverts `Where::signature` back to `SyntaxShape::RowCondition` and updates `SyntaxShape::RowCondition`'s Display impl instead.

defect: get_alias_documentation prints `let alias_name = &sig.name;` as the alias heading (`Alias: <name>`), where `sig` is obtained from `engine_state.get_signature(command)`. Because `Alias::signature()` in crates/nu-protocol/src/alias.rs delegates to the wrapped target command's signature for internal-command aliases, `help <alias>` displays the target command's name instead of `command.name()` (the actual alias name).
trigger: Defining an alias to an internal command (e.g. `alias ll = ls -l`) and running `help ll`.
match_rule: Identify that `get_alias_documentation` uses `sig.name` instead of `command.name()`, and `Alias::signature()` returns the wrapped target command's signature/name rather than the alias's own name.
near_misses: Flagging alias expansion formatting or backtick highlighting without identifying `sig.name` vs `command.name()` via `Alias::signature()`.
why_findable: 6fba4b40 adds `get_alias_documentation` reading `&sig.name` from `engine_state.get_signature(command)`, while `Alias::signature()` in crates/nu-protocol/src/alias.rs delegates to the aliased command's signature whereas `Alias::name()` returns the alias name.
notes: Fix commit 644ea6ea switches `get_alias_documentation` to `command.name()`.

defect: map_value_completions applies custom/external completers' returned `span: { start, end }` directly as raw reedline buffer offsets (`reedline::Span { start: start.min(end), end }`) without adding the start offset of the command expression being completed. Because NuCompleter slices `context` to only the current command expression before invoking the completer (e.g. passing `"bar ba"` for `foo | bar ba`), a completer returning `{ start: 0, end: 6 }` replaces the prefix `"foo | "` at the start of the buffer instead of `"bar ba"`.
trigger: Invoking a custom or external completer that returns an explicit `span` record inside a pipeline or subexpression, e.g. `foo | bar ba<TAB>` returning `{ start: 0, end: 6 }`.
match_rule: Identify that `map_value_completions` interprets custom/external completer `span` records as absolute buffer indices instead of offsetting them by the command expression's start position (despite the completer receiving only the sliced command expression as context).
near_misses: Flagging only `start > end` clamping or missing half-span overrides without identifying the coordinate mismatch between expression-relative completer input and buffer-absolute replacement span.
why_findable: ca602772f writes `suggestion.span = reedline::Span { start: start.min(end), end }` directly in `map_value_completions` without any expression offset, while `NuCompleter::complete_with_working_set` in the same file slices `line` at `element_expression.span.start - offset` before passing it to completers.
notes: Fix commit 2b6d24c3 shifts custom/external completer override spans by the command expression start offset.

defect: extract_semantic_tokens_from_expression switched from checking working_set.get_span_contents(call.head) to working_set.get_decl(call.decl_id).name() for spaces; module-imported commands like `use std/assert; assert equal` store only the unprefixed declaration name (`equal`) without spaces, so their multi-word call heads no longer receive LSP semantic tokens.
trigger: Request textDocument/semanticTokens/full in nu-lsp for a script calling a module-prefixed command such as `use std/assert; assert equal`.
match_rule: Identifies that semantic_tokens.rs checks `working_set.get_decl(call.decl_id).name().contains(' ')` instead of the source text at `call.head`, which misses module-prefixed commands whose declaration name omits the module prefix.
near_misses: Complaining about `export`/`overlay` exclusions or the `flat_map` mutable accumulator refactor without identifying the `decl.name()` vs `call.head` mismatch for module-prefixed commands.
why_findable: Comparing `extract_semantic_tokens_from_expression` in nu-lsp with how module-imported commands register their `Decl::name()` in nu-parser/nu-protocol shows that module prefixes appear in `call.head` source bytes but not in `decl.name()`.
notes: Clean regression in #15567 (`e5f589ccdd`); previously `get_span_contents(call.head)` was used and preserved module-prefixed commands.

defect: Stack stores `error_handlers` (catch) and `finally_run_handlers` (finally) on two separate stacks and `eval_ir_block_impl` always pops `error_handlers` before `finally_run_handlers` (and returns immediately on `ShellError::Break`/`Continue`), so an error inside a nested `try { ... } finally { ... }` jumps straight to an outer `catch` skipping the inner `finally`, and `break`/`continue` inside `try { ... } finally { ... }` skips `finally` and leaves stale handlers behind.
trigger: Evaluate `try { try { error make { msg: 'a' } } finally { print 'inner' } } catch { print 'outer' }` or `for x in [1 2] { try { break } finally { print 'f' } }`.
match_rule: Identifies that keeping `catch` and `finally` on separate stacks (`error_handlers` vs `finally_run_handlers`) and prioritizing `error_handlers.pop` in `eval_ir_block_impl` (plus bypassing `finally_run_handlers` on `Break`/`Continue`) skips inner `finally` blocks when unwinding to an outer `catch` or loop.
near_misses: Mentioning only `exit` (which was explicitly noted as follow-up work in the commit message) without identifying the separate-stack ordering bug for nested `try`/`finally`/`catch` or `break`/`continue`.
why_findable: Tracing `compile_try` (`OnError` + `Finally` instructions) against `Stack::{error_handlers, finally_run_handlers}` in `nu-protocol` and error unwinding in `eval_ir_block_impl` (`nu-engine`) directly reveals that an outer `error_handlers` entry shadows an inner `finally_run_handlers` entry and that `Break`/`Continue` bypass `finally_run_handlers`.
notes: Commit message only flagged `exit` as follow-up; nested `try/finally` under outer `catch` and `break`/`continue` unwinding were unflagged defects introduced by #17397.

defect: In `TryFrom<DebouncedEvent> for WatchEvent`, the `RenameMode::Both` arm reversed `ev.paths` with `.drain(..).rev().next_array()` before binding `[from, to]`, swapping `path` (source) and `new_path` (destination) on every rename event.
trigger: Run `watch` on a directory and rename a file (`mv foo.txt bar.txt`); the emitted `Rename` event reports `path: bar.txt` and `new_path: foo.txt` instead of `path: foo.txt` and `new_path: bar.txt`.
match_rule: Identifies that `ev.paths.drain(..).rev().next_array()` reverses notify's `[from, to]` path order, causing `WatchEvent { path: from, new_path: Some(to) }` to swap old and new paths.
near_misses: Commenting only on missing `RenameMode::From`/`To` handling (which sits under an existing `TODO` comment) without catching the `.rev()` path swap on `RenameMode::Both`.
why_findable: Directly visible in `TryFrom<DebouncedEvent>::try_from`: notify stores `[from, to]` in order (which the prior two-`.pop()` code popped as `to` then `from`), so adding `.rev()` reversed the pair.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`); the `.rev()` swap was newly introduced when #16428 refactored `watch` from two `.pop()` calls into `TryFrom<DebouncedEvent>`.

defect: Moving `ensure_not_reserved_variable_name` (`in`, `nu`, `env`) from `parse_def_inner` into `parse_signature_helper` caused `extern` and `export extern` declarations (which share `SyntaxShape::Signature`) to reject external CLI parameter and flag names like `in`, `--env`, or `...nu` with `ParseError::NameIsBuiltinVar`.
trigger: Parse an external command signature using a builtin variable name as a parameter or flag, e.g. `extern cmd [in, --env]` or `export extern cmd (in, --env, ...nu)`.
match_rule: Identifies that `parse_signature_helper` runs `ensure_not_reserved_variable_name` unconditionally for all `SyntaxShape::Signature` callers, including `Extern` and `ExportExtern` signatures that do not bind Nushell variables.
near_misses: Flagging `let`/`mut`/`for` reserved variable checks or complaining about `it` being allowed, without noticing that `extern`/`export extern` share `parse_signature_helper` via `SyntaxShape::Signature`.
why_findable: Following callers of `parse_signature_helper` (`parse_full_signature` / `SyntaxShape::Signature`) across `nu-parser` and `nu-cmd-lang` (`Extern`, `ExportExtern`) shows that `extern` signatures now inherit the reserved-variable check previously scoped to `parse_def_inner`.
notes: Before #17741 (`46804de038`), reserved variable name checks ran only in `parse_def_inner`, leaving `parse_extern` unaffected.

defect: `parse_export_in_block` calls `warp_export_call` with `&lite_command.parts` (which includes leading attribute tokens rather than `lite_command.command_parts()`), and `warp_export_call`'s `Expr::AttributeBlock` arm overwrites `def_call.head` with `Span::concat(&spans[0..=1])`, replacing the `export def`/`export extern` head span with the attribute span.
trigger:
Parse a top-level attributed export command such as `@category foo
export def foo [] {}` or `@complete external
export extern bar []` and inspect `def_call.head` (e.g. via LSP document highlight on `export def`).
match_rule: Identifies that `parse_export_in_block` passes `&lite_command.parts` (including attribute tokens) to `warp_export_call`, whose `Expr::AttributeBlock` branch overwrites `ab.item`'s `def_call.head = Span::concat(&spans[0..=1])` with the attribute spans instead of preserving the `export def`/`export extern` span set by `parse_def_inner`/`parse_extern_inner`.
near_misses: Noting only the `TODO` comment on `warp_export_call` being clumsy without identifying the `&lite_command.parts` vs `command_parts()` span corruption of `def_call.head` on attributed exports.
why_findable: Comparing `parse_export_in_block` (passing `&lite_command.parts`) with `LiteCommand::command_parts()` in `lite_parser.rs` and `parse_export_in_module` (passing `lite_command.command_parts()`) reveals that `spans[0..=1]` in `warp_export_call` points to attribute tokens whenever `Expr::AttributeBlock` is present.
notes: Introduced in #16696 (`d414ebb827`), which added `warp_export_call` to `parse_export_in_block`; `parse_def_inner`/`parse_extern_inner` already computed `def_call.head` from `command_parts()`.

defect: In `extract_formatting_operations`, the `batching` closure checks `it.peek()?` at the top and returns `None` when the iterator is exhausted; when a pattern ends with an unmatched `{` (e.g. `"{"`, `"hello {"`, `"{name}{"`), the `'{'` arm sets `is_fixed = false` and returns `FixedText`, and the next iteration exits via `it.peek()?` before reaching the `if !is_fixed { Some(Err(())) }` check, silently dropping the unmatched `{` instead of returning `ShellError::DelimiterError`.
trigger: Run `{} | format pattern '{'`, `{} | format pattern 'hello {'`, or `{} | format pattern '{name}{'`; it succeeds instead of returning `ShellError::DelimiterError`.
match_rule: Identifies that returning `FixedText` on `'{'` with `is_fixed = false` followed by `let start_index = it.peek()?.0;` at the start of the `batching` closure terminates the iterator without emitting an unmatched-brace error when `{` is the final character.
near_misses: Flagging span derivation for escaped strings or variables (which are already explicitly noted in `NOTE:` comments) without catching the `it.peek()?` early return on trailing `{`.
why_findable: Directly visible inside `extract_formatting_operations` by tracing the `batching` iterator state when `{` is the last character in `pattern`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`); before #16899 (`b093457273`), `column_span_end < column_span_start` returned `DelimiterError` for trailing `{`. Note `cf5390edc5` also fixed a separate pre-2025 trailing `{` bug in `parse`.

defect: In `NuCompleter::complete_expression`, when an `Expr::ExternalCall` argument receives no suggestions from `sudo`/`doas` or an external completer, the branch breaks out to the generic fallback, which runs `strip_placeholder_with_rsplit(working_set, &element_expression.span, |c| *c == b' ')`, splitting inside quoted/backticked path arguments containing spaces instead of completing against the argument's own span.
trigger: Request tab completion on an external command with a backtick-quoted path argument containing spaces, e.g. ``foo `dir with space/` ``.
match_rule: Identifies that `Expr::ExternalCall` breaks to the fallback calling `strip_placeholder_with_rsplit(&element_expression.span, |c| *c == b' ')`, which splits inside path arguments containing spaces instead of using the matched argument's `span`.
near_misses: Blaming `FileCompletion` quoting logic or external completer config without noticing that `complete_expression` discards the external argument `span` and splits `element_expression.span` on ASCII spaces.
why_findable: Directly visible in `complete_expression`: the `Expr::ExternalCall` arm already locates the active argument `span`, then breaks out and lets lines 376-383 split the entire command span on `b' '`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`); before #15086 (`be508cbd7f`), flattened expression completion passed the exact argument span to `FileCompletion`.

defect: Replacing `get_full_help` with hardcoded ANSI-colored `cli_help_text()` in `parse_cli_args` caused `nu --help` to write raw ANSI escape sequences to stdout even when stdout is redirected to a pipe or file instead of a terminal.
trigger: Run `nu --help` with stdout redirected (non-TTY, e.g. `nu --help | cat` or captured `Command::output()`).
match_rule: Identifies that `parse_cli_args` prints `cli_help_text()`, which embeds ANSI color constants unconditionally without checking `stdout().is_terminal()` or stripping ANSI sequences for non-TTY output.
near_misses: Flagging help text wording or flag parsing in `lexopt` without noticing that `cli_help_text()` emits ANSI escapes unconditionally when stdout is not a terminal.
why_findable: Visible in `src/command.rs`: `cli_help_text()` hardcodes `HELP_SECTION_COLOR` (`\x1b[32m`) etc. and `parse_cli_args` writes it straight to stdout without any terminal check, regressing `get_full_help`'s `UseAnsiColoring::Auto` behavior.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`); before #17405 (`1fa0f68884`), `get_full_help` stripped ANSI via `use_ansi_coloring.get(engine_state)` (default `Auto` -> `is_terminal()`).

defect: Although `fcfda921c5` added `semver`/`semver-range` default colors and `Value::Custom` dispatch in `StyleComputer::style_primitive`, `build_table_batch` in `crates/nu-command/src/viewers/table.rs` still unconditionally converts every `Value::Custom` element to its base value (`Value::String` for `SemVer`) before calling `nu-table`, bypassing `StyleComputer`'s `Value::Custom` branch and stripping `semver` colors from lists displayed by `table`.
trigger: Run `$env.config.use_ansi_coloring = true; ['1.0.0' '2.0.0'] | into semver | table`; the rendered table cells use plain string styling instead of `semver` cyan_bold (`\x1b[1;36m`).
match_rule: Identifies that `build_table_batch` eagerly replaces every `Value::Custom` element with `custom.to_base_value(span)` (a `Value::String` for `SemVer`), so `StyleComputer::style_primitive`'s newly added `Value::Custom` branch never receives primitive custom values when rendering lists in `table`.
near_misses: Complaining about `color_config` parsing or `SemVer::type_name()` without connecting `StyleComputer::style_primitive`'s `Value::Custom` arm to `build_table_batch` eagerly collapsing `Value::Custom` to `to_base_value()`.
why_findable: Tracing how `table` renders a list of `SemVer` custom values from `nu-command/src/viewers/table.rs` (`build_table_batch`) into `nu-table` and `nu-color-config/src/style_computer.rs` (`style_primitive`) immediately exposes that `build_table_batch` converts `Value::Custom` to `Value::String` before styling.
notes: Cross-crate relation between `nu-color-config` and `nu-command` (`table.rs` + `semver/value.rs`); `7adc2ade0e`'s `build_table_batch` fix and `table_semver_list_colors` test survived untouched in later commits.

defect: Replacing ureq's `DefaultConnector::default()` with a standalone `InterruptibleTcpConnector` in `http_client_pool` and `http_client` removed `SocksConnector` and `ConnectProxyConnector` from the connector chain, and `InterruptibleTcpConnector::connect` ignores `_chained: Option<In>` instead of forwarding an already-connected proxy transport, causing `http` commands to ignore `ALL_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables even though `config_builder.proxy(...)` still sets them.
trigger: Set `ALL_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, or `HTTPS_PROXY` to a SOCKS5 (or HTTP CONNECT) proxy URI and run `http get --raw <url>`; `http` bypasses the proxy and dials `<url>` directly.
match_rule: Identifies that `http_client` and `http_client_pool` configure `config_builder.proxy(...)` from proxy env vars but pass bare `InterruptibleTcpConnector` (omitting `SocksConnector` and `ConnectProxyConnector`), and that `InterruptibleTcpConnector::connect` ignores `_chained` rather than passing through chained proxy transports.
near_misses: Flagging `retrieve_http_proxy_from_env` or `InterruptibleUnixSocketConnector` without identifying that `client.rs` dropped `SocksConnector`/`ConnectProxyConnector` from the `ureq::Agent::with_parts` connector chain and `InterruptibleTcpConnector::connect` ignores `_chained`.
why_findable: Comparing `http_client_pool`/`http_client` (`client.rs`, which still configures `config_builder.proxy(Some(proxy))` before replacing `DefaultConnector::default()` with `InterruptibleTcpConnector`) against `InterruptibleTcpConnector`'s `Connector<In>` impl (`interruptible_tcp.rs`, ignoring `_chained`) and ureq's `DefaultConnector` chain shows that proxy connectors are both omitted and unchainable.
notes: Clean multi-file regression in #17507 (`0b4639fde7`); at `0b4639fde7^`, `DefaultConnector::default()` chained `SocksConnector` + `ConnectProxyConnector` + `TcpConnector` + TLS so plain HTTP over SOCKS5 (`http_get_with_socks5_proxy`) worked.

defect: In parse_source, replacing `parse_value(working_set, spans[1], &SyntaxShape::Any)` with `call.positional_nth(0)` from `parse_internal_call` switches `source`'s filename parsing from `SyntaxShape::Any` (which falls through to `parse_string`) to `Source::signature`'s `SyntaxShape::OneOf([Filepath, Nothing])` -> `parse_filepath`. Because `parse_filepath` only calls `unescape_unquote_string` and omits `parse_string`'s bare-word interpolation check (`bytes.contains(&b'(')` -> `parse_string_interpolation`), bare-word interpolated paths like `source test_($nu.os-info.name).nu` are parsed as literal `Expr::Filepath` strings instead of `Expr::StringInterpolation` and fail with file-not-found.
trigger: Running `source` with a bare-word interpolated constant path, e.g. `source test_($nu.os-info.name).nu`.
match_rule: Identify that changing `parse_source` from `parse_value(..., &SyntaxShape::Any)` to `call.positional_nth(0)` parses `source`'s filename argument via `Source::signature`'s `SyntaxShape::Filepath` (`parse_filepath`) instead of `parse_string`, which lacks bare-word string interpolation (`(`) handling and therefore treats interpolated bare-word paths like `source config/($nu.os-info.name).nu` as literal filenames.
near_misses: Complaining generally about `ArgumentParsingLevel::FirstK`, `parse_import_pattern`, or `source-env` (which uses `SyntaxShape::String`) without identifying that `source`'s `SyntaxShape::Filepath` (`parse_filepath`) drops bare-word interpolation previously handled by `SyntaxShape::Any` -> `parse_string`.
why_findable: 245c09b27 replaces `parse_value(working_set, spans[1], &SyntaxShape::Any)` with `call.positional_nth(0)` in `parse_source`, while `Source::signature` in `crates/nu-command/src/misc/source.rs` declares `filename` as `SyntaxShape::OneOf(vec![SyntaxShape::Filepath, SyntaxShape::Nothing])` and `parse_filepath` in `crates/nu-parser/src/parser.rs` lacks the bare-word `(` interpolation branch present in `parse_string`.
notes: Clean cross-crate regression in #16403 (`245c09b27c`, released in 0.109.0, fixed in 0.109.1 hotfix #17094 `cde5f7be8c` by adding the bare-word interpolation check to `parse_filepath`).
